title: Three Mornings and One Short Staff
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：kung fu　|　正文 357 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 kung fu 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the master ① practised the kung fu that no student in the courtyard would have described, and he said the practising was the whole of the morning. The ② kung fu, meaning the skill itself and not the staff, ran three mornings and stayed undescribed in the book; kung fu, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ form of kung fu in that courtyard had the same short staff beside it, and the ④ kung fu at the far gate, meaning the form they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. Kung fu, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the master said the describing is the part that fills three mornings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the kung fu was the whole of the matter, meaning the discipline and not the skill. The ⑥ kung fu, meaning the discipline and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; kung fu, he said, is either something you practise or the only word that means both skill and a discipline. He said the discipline is the part they remember.

By 1963 the ⑦ kung fu had become a line in a manual, and the manual had become an argument about the short staff. The ⑧ kung fu of the whole thing, the master wrote in October, was one courtyard and three mornings of describing; kung fu, he said, is either the form at the far gate or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ kung fu I remember is the kung fu described in the manual, which closed in 1965 and is still described as the quietest in the courtyard. ⑩ Kung fu, my mother said in 1967, is the only thing that improves by being described; all kung fu, she said, is a discipline that has agreed to look like skill. She said the discipline was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 功夫；武艺（指院子里每一门旁边的那一门）
B. n. 功夫；武艺（指那门功夫本身，与木棍相对）
C. 固定搭配：practise the kung fu 练这门功夫
D. n. 功夫；武艺（指留给孩子们照练的那一套那一门）
E. n. 习武之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的功夫之事）
F. n. 功夫；武艺（指拳谱里写到、被记述的的那一门）
G. n. 规矩、修习（指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 修习（抽象总称，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: practised the kung fu that no student in the courtyard would have described
The kung fu, meaning the skill itself and not the staff
Every form of kung fu in that courtyard
the kung fu at the far gate
the kung fu was the whole of the matter
The kung fu, meaning the discipline
the kung fu had become a line in a manual
The kung fu of the whole thing
Kung fu, my mother said in 1967

answers.why: practise the kung fu 意为“练这门功夫”，1958 年那位师父把院子里没有一位弟子肯记述的一门功夫做了一遍。
kung fu 意为“功夫；武艺”，指那门功夫本身而不是木棍，它经过了三个早晨而在簿子上没有被记述。
kung fu 意为“功夫；武艺”，指院子里每一门旁边的那一门，每一门旁边都有同一根短短的木棍。
kung fu 意为“功夫；武艺”，指最远那道门边留给孩子们照练的那一套那一门，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
kung fu 意为“规矩、修习”，指一件事里人人都练却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这套规矩就是那件事的全部。
kung fu 意为“修习”，指人人都练却无人提起的那样东西而不是那门功夫，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
kung fu 意为“功夫；武艺”，指拳谱里写到、被记述的的那一门，到 1963 年这一门成了拳谱里的一行。
kung fu 意为“习武之事”，师父十月写道，整件事的功夫之事是一处院子和三个早晨的记述。
kung fu 意为“功夫；武艺”，我记得的是拳谱里记述过的那一门，1965 年练成了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一门。
kung fu 为抽象总称，母亲 1967 年说，功夫是唯一会因为被好好记述而变得更好的功夫。

那门功夫，指的是那门功夫本身而不是木棍，经过了三个早晨而在簿子上没有被记述。（kung fu）
那处院子里每一门功夫旁边都有同一根短短的木棍。（kung fu）
